items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep.

items.label: Control Locks
items.info: Control column. Click the control lock to remove it. Chocks and the rudder lock are removed in the EFB's parking mode. Leaving a lock in will jam the flight controls.

items.label: All Switches
items.info: All panels. Clean electrical state before battery power is applied.

items.label: Circuit Breakers
items.info: Lower panel. All breakers pushed in — no circuits isolated.

items.label: Alternate Air Controls
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Confirms the alternate induction air doors are in the normal (closed) position.

items.label: Landing Gear Switch
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Handle must match the weight-on-wheels state before power-up.

items.label: Fuel Selectors
items.info: Between the seats. Each engine feeds from its respective main tank.

items.label: Emergency Crossfeed Shutoff
items.info: Between the seats. Open for normal operation. Closed only for a fire or a wheels-up landing, when it isolates the crossfeed lines from the tanks.

items.label: Battery
items.info: Left panel. Powers the electrical buses so instruments and warning lights come alive.

items.label: Annunciator Panel
items.info: Main panel. Press and hold the annunciator test button. All warning and caution lights should illuminate, confirming bulbs are functional.

items.label: Fuel Gauges
items.info: Main panel. Verify operation and quantity on all tanks.

items.label: Landing Gear Lights
items.info: Main panel. Three green lights confirm all gear are down and locked.

items.label: NAV Light
items.info: Left panel. Position lights on wingtips and tail.

items.label: Battery
items.info: Left panel. Off after preflight checks are complete — restarted during engine start sequence.

items.label: Fuel Selectors
items.info: Between the seats. Confirm both on main tanks before start.

items.label: Cabin Door
items.info: Annunciator panel. The red DOOR WARN light stays on until the main cabin door is secured for flight.

items.label: Prop Synchrophaser
items.info: Main panel. Must be off before start — only activated in cruise once both engines are running.

items.label: Yaw Damper
items.info: Center pedestal on the Navomatic (YD toggle switch), or the YD key on the GFC600. Off for start and taxi; it goes on after takeoff.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Cracked slightly for the engine to catch without surging.

items.label: Propellers
items.info: Center pedestal. Full fine pitch for maximum RPM governing during start.

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. Full forward for start. Keep the auto mixture assist in the sim options disabled; the aircraft has its own fuel controller. On Xbox auto mixture is forced on and the levers can be ignored.

items.label: Battery
items.info: Left panel. Powers the starter and ignition circuits.

items.label: Alternators
items.info: Left panel. Arms both alternators to charge the battery once engines are running.

items.label: Fuel Computer
items.info: Engine panel. Enter the usable fuel on board before each flight. The computer counts down from that figure, so a wrong entry gives a wrong fuel remaining and range. Update it after refuelling.

items.label: Beacon
items.info: Left panel, ANTI-COLL switch. The only anti-collision light switch; there is no separate strobe switch. On before engine start to warn ground crew.

items.label: Cowl Flaps
items.info: Center pedestal. Open for cooling during ground running and takeoff. Closed cowl flaps let the cylinder heads overheat.

items.label: Magnetos
items.info: Side console. All magneto switches ON, left and right engine.

items.label: Primer
items.info: Side console. Prime the left engine briefly before cranking. Needed when the engine is cold.

items.label: Left Engine
items.info: Side console. Hold the left starter until the engine fires.

items.label: Primer
items.info: Side console. Prime the right engine briefly before cranking. Needed when the engine is cold.

items.label: Right Engine
items.info: Side console. Hold the right starter until the engine fires.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Warm-up range. Oil pressure must reach 25 PSI within 30 seconds.

items.label: Oil Pressure
items.info: Engine panel. At least 25 PSI within 30 seconds of start. No pressure: shut the engine down.

items.label: Alternators
items.info: Left panel. Confirm both alternators are carrying a positive load after start.

items.label: Avionics Master Switch
items.info: Left panel. Powers the avionics bus now that voltage is stable.

items.label: Avionics & GPS
items.info: Main panel. Program frequencies, set GPS flight plan, verify navigation sources.

items.label: Transponder
items.info: Main panel. Dial in squawk code and leave in standby until ready for departure.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: Main panel. Set local pressure from ATIS or tower.

items.label: Trim Tabs
items.info: Center pedestal. Elevator set for takeoff, rudder and aileron to neutral.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. Up for taxi.

items.label: Flight Controls
items.info: Yoke and pedals. Full deflection in all axes to confirm no restrictions.

items.label: Taxi Lights
items.info: Left panel. Illuminates the taxiway ahead.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Release and begin taxi. Check braking and steering.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Hold firmly for run-up power checks.

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. Full rich. The fuel controller holds fuel flow, so no leaning is needed.

items.label: Propellers
items.info: Center pedestal. Fine pitch for maximum RPM during magneto checks.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Run-up power for magneto and system checks.

items.label: Magnetos
items.info: Side console. At run-up RPM, switch off one magneto at a time and back on. The engine should keep running smoothly with only a small RPM drop.

items.label: Propellers
items.info: Center pedestal. Pull each propeller lever into feather until the RPM starts to fall, then back to full forward. Confirms the governor and feathering work.

items.label: Engine Instruments
items.info: Main panel. All indications in the green arcs before returning to 1000 RPM.

items.label: Vacuum System
items.info: Pilot lower panel, suction gauge. Powers the gyro instruments. A red marker in the gauge means that engine’s vacuum source is inoperative.

items.label: HYD FLOW Lights
items.info: Main panel. L & R HYD FLOW warning lights should be extinguished at run-up power, confirming both hydraulic pumps are operating.

items.label: Battery Load
items.info: Left panel. Ammeter selector to BATT position. Confirm zero load — the alternators should be carrying the full electrical bus with no remaining draw from the battery.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Back to 1000 RPM once the run-up checks are done.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Release after the run-up checks are complete.

items.label: Fuel Selectors
items.info: Between the seats. Confirm both on main tanks.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. Normal takeoff is flaps up. Clean configuration provides best climb performance.

items.label: Trim Tabs
items.info: Center pedestal. Confirm elevator, rudder, and aileron set.

items.label: Ram Dump
items.info: Pilot lower panel, DUMP PULL RAM knob. Pulled out, it dumps cabin pressure and the cabin will not pressurize.

items.label: Pressurization
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Mode switch to PRESSURIZE and set the cabin altitude controller.

items.label: Aux Fuel Pumps
items.info: Side console. Backup fuel pressure for the critical takeoff phase.

items.label: Pitot Heat
items.info: Left panel. Prevents pitot icing that would corrupt airspeed readings. A placard requires it on below 40°F (4°C) in instrument conditions.

items.label: Anti-Ice
items.info: Left panel. PROP ANTI-ICE, ANTI-ICE ELECT (HI or LO), SURFACE DE-ICE and STALL & VENT HEAT on as needed when flying into visible moisture at freezing temperatures. There is no engine anti-ice.

items.label: Air Conditioning
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Off or recirculate for takeoff. The compressor runs off the hydraulic system; the green A COND HYD light shows when it is running.

items.label: Transponder
items.info: Main panel. Active for ATC radar identification at line-up.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Left panel. Visibility for traffic avoidance during takeoff roll and climb.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Hold the brakes and bring both throttles up together. Check both manifold pressure needles rise evenly before brake release.

items.label: Brakes
items.info: Rudder pedals. Release toe brakes and begin the takeoff roll.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Advance smoothly to max 41 inHg MP. The TSIO-520 is turbocharged, so avoid slamming the throttles.

items.label: Rotate
items.info: Yoke. Rotate gently with flaps up, keeping well above the red line (Vmca) on the airspeed indicator.

items.label: Gear
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Retract at positive rate of climb. Vlo is 177 KIAS.

items.label: Climb Power
items.info: Center pedestal. Reduce from takeoff power: throttles back first, then propellers. Keep manifold pressure in the green arc. Full manifold pressure is for takeoff only; holding it too long overheats the engines and costs power.

items.label: Autopilot
items.info: Center pedestal on the Navomatic: AP toggle switch ON. With the GFC600, press the AP key.

items.label: Taxi Lights
items.info: Left panel. No longer needed once airborne.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Left panel. LDG switch to RETRACT, which stows the retractable landing lights. OFF only switches them off.

items.label: Aux Fuel Pumps
items.info: Side console. Keep on LOW during climb as backup fuel pressure.

items.label: Cowl Flaps
items.info: Center pedestal. Open as needed to keep CHT in the green during climb.

items.label: Cabin Altitude
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Dial in the planned cruise altitude on the cabin altitude controller.

items.label: Yaw Damper
items.info: Center pedestal on the Navomatic (YD toggle switch), or the YD key on the GFC600. Damps the yawing oscillation the aircraft can develop at altitude. Set and forget.

items.label: Anti-Ice
items.info: Left panel. PROP ANTI-ICE, ANTI-ICE ELECT (HI or LO), SURFACE DE-ICE and STALL & VENT HEAT on as needed when climbing through visible moisture at freezing temperatures. With visible ice on the aircraft, stay below 185 KIAS (placard).

items.label: Air Conditioning
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Restore A/C once established in the climb and clear of the takeoff power segment.

items.label: Oxygen
items.info: Pilot lower panel, EMER OXY PULL knob and oxygen cylinder gauge. Needed when cabin altitude exceeds 10,000 ft; the amber CABIN ALT light comes on above that. Pressurization normally keeps the cabin well below it.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: Main panel. Set to standard pressure (29.92 / 1013) at transition altitude.

items.label: Cruise Power
items.info: Center pedestal. Typical: High ~78–84% (34.0 inHG / 2300 RPM), Normal ~72–76% (31.5 inHG / 2450 RPM), Economy ~52–56% (25 inHG / 2200 RPM).

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. No leaning needed. A fuel controller holds fuel flow at any altitude, including above the 21,000 ft critical altitude, so the mixture can stay rich for most of the flight. Keep the sim’s auto mixture disabled.

items.label: Prop Synchrophaser
items.info: Main panel. Synchronizes both propeller RPMs to eliminate the irritating beat frequency in the cabin.

items.label: Cowl Flaps
items.info: Center pedestal. Close once CHT is stable in the green to reduce drag.

items.label: Pressurization
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Verify cabin altitude is holding at the set level. Maximum differential is 5.3 PSI.

items.label: Aux Fuel Pumps
items.info: Side console. Can be turned off in stable cruise unless fuel flow fluctuations occur.

items.label: Oxygen
items.info: Pilot lower panel, oxygen cylinder gauge. On if cabin altitude exceeds 10,000 ft.

items.label: Anti-Ice
items.info: Left panel. Monitor outside air temperature and visible moisture. PROP ANTI-ICE, ANTI-ICE ELECT (HI or LO), SURFACE DE-ICE and STALL & VENT HEAT on as needed.

items.label: Descent Power
items.info: Center pedestal. Reduce power gradually, throttles first, keeping manifold pressure in the green arc. A sudden power cut from high altitude cools the cylinders too fast.

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. Watch EGT while descending from high altitude into warmer air and adjust the mixture to keep it steady. Letting it swing can crack a cylinder head.

items.label: Cabin Altitude
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Set the destination field elevation on the cabin altitude controller so the cabin equalizes smoothly before landing.

items.label: Aux Fuel Pumps
items.info: Side console. Backup fuel pressure for the approach and landing phases.

items.label: Cowl Flaps
items.info: Center pedestal. Closed during descent unless CHT climbs out of the green.

items.label: Oxygen
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Off once cabin altitude is confirmed below 10,000 ft.

items.label: Anti-Ice
items.info: Left panel. PROP ANTI-ICE, ANTI-ICE ELECT (HI or LO), SURFACE DE-ICE and STALL & VENT HEAT on as needed when descending through visible moisture at freezing temperatures.

items.label: Altimeters
items.info: Main panel. Set local pressure passing the transition level.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Left panel. On below 10,000 ft for traffic visibility.

items.label: Prop Synchrophaser
items.info: Main panel. Off before landing. Not needed at low speeds and must be off for go-around.

items.label: Propellers
items.info: Center pedestal. Full fine pitch for immediate go-around power.

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. Full rich for maximum power availability on go-around.

items.label: Yaw Damper
items.info: Center pedestal on the Navomatic (YD toggle switch), or the YD key on the GFC600. Off for landing; the pilot needs full rudder authority for crosswind corrections.

items.label: Approach Mode
items.info: Autopilot panel. GFC600: press APR; the mode shows armed, then active on capture. Navomatic 800B: press NAV with the localizer tuned; the glideslope engages by itself at beam center when approached from below.

items.label: Anti-Ice
items.info: Left panel. Check PROP ANTI-ICE, ANTI-ICE ELECT (HI or LO), SURFACE DE-ICE and STALL & VENT HEAT are set for the conditions.

items.label: Speed
items.info: Throttles, center pedestal. Slow down before the first flap and gear extension. Flaps 15 are limited to 171 KIAS and the gear to 177 KIAS.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. First flap setting. Limit for flaps 15 is 171 KIAS (placard by the flap selector).

items.label: Gear
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Extend below 177 KIAS. Confirm three green lights.

items.label: Speed
items.info: Throttles, center pedestal. Limit for flaps beyond 15 degrees is 140 KIAS (placard by the flap selector). Slow down before flaps 30.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. Only below 140 KIAS. Set on glideslope intercept or base leg.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. Full flaps at 1000 ft AGL on the glideslope or on final. Limit is 140 KIAS.

items.label: Autopilot
items.info: Pilot yoke. Press the AP disconnect button, which trips the autopilot master switch, and hand-fly the final approach and landing.

items.label: Speed
items.info: Yoke and throttles. Stable final approach speed with full flaps: below the 140 KIAS flap limit and well above the red line (Vmca).

items.label: Landing Gear
items.info: Main panel. Final confirmation of three green lights before the threshold.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Slowly retard at the threshold. Gently flare and touch down on the main gear first.

items.label: Taxi Lights
items.info: Left panel. Illuminate the taxiway for the taxi to parking.

items.label: Landing Lights
items.info: Left panel. LDG switch to RETRACT once clear of the runway, which stows the retractable landing lights.

items.label: Flaps
items.info: Copilot lower panel. Retract to prevent ground damage during taxi.

items.label: Transponder
items.info: Main panel. Back to standby once clear of the active.

items.label: Cowl Flaps
items.info: Center pedestal. Open to cool the engines during taxi.

items.label: Parking Brake
items.info: Pilot lower panel. Hold the aircraft at the gate.

items.label: Avionics Master Switch
items.info: Left panel. Power down radios and GPS before cutting battery.

items.label: Aux Fuel Pumps
items.info: Side console. No longer needed with engines about to stop.

items.label: Throttles
items.info: Center pedestal. Confirm at idle before mixture cutoff.

items.label: Mixtures
items.info: Center pedestal. Pull both mixture levers to cutoff for a clean shutdown.

items.label: Magnetos
items.info: Side console. All magneto switches, left and right engine, to OFF after the props stop turning.

items.label: Battery & Alternators
items.info: Left panel. Master battery and both alternator switches off.

items.label: Fuel Selectors
items.info: Between the seats. Shut off fuel flow to prevent leaks while parked.

items.label: Emergency Crossfeed Shutoff
items.info: Between the seats. Isolates the crossfeed lines from the tanks while the aircraft is parked.

items.label: Control Locks
items.info: Yoke and pedals. Prevents wind damage to control surfaces while parked.

description: A pressurized, turbocharged piston twin with a 30,000 ft service ceiling and about 1,100 NM of range for serious cross-country trips.
